To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
highly persistent carcinogen-DNA covalent adduction occurs in mouse skin and may be a critical factor in the initiation of skin carcinogenesis.
highly persistent PAH-DNA adduct levels in skin were detected using a sensitive, specific 32P-postlabelling method.

1) highly persistent PAH-DNA adduct levels were observed in mouse skin DNA; 2) the levels of these adducts were similar to those observed in human lung DNA from smokers; and 3) the levels of adducts in the DNA from mouse skin were similar to the levels of addducts in DNA from mouse lung.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAH-DNA adduct profile in mouse skin is highly complex and the adduct levels are highly persistent.
the 32P-postlabelling technique can be used to determine the amount of carcinogen-DNA binding and to detect the presence of carcinogen-DNAs adducts in skin DNA of treated mice.
PAH-DNA adduct levels in mouse skin decline rapidly in the first 2 to 3 weeks after carcinogen exposure and thereafter persist at low levels in the DNA of quiescent cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
persistent DNA adducts may play an important role in the initiation of skin carcinogenesis by PAHs.
the DNA adducts formed in mouse skin after application of PAHs are highly persistent and may be present at specific genomic sites.
the 32P-postlabelling method can be applied to the analysis of PAH-DNA adduct formation and persistence in mouse skin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA adduct levels can persist for weeks after exposure to carcinogenic PAHs.
the 32P-postlabelling technique is a very sensitive and versatile method for the detection of carcinogen-DNA binding.
the 32P-postlabelling method can be used to study DNA damage in skin and that the method is sensitive enough to detect DNA adducts that persist in the genome of quiescent cells.
